articleTitle: Simultaneous Measurement of Space Charge Distribution and Leakage Current in 6.6 kV CV Cable Under Polarity-Reversed Voltage
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental study on temporal changes in space charge distribution in a 6.6 kV CV cable and associated dc leakage current under high temperature. A test sample is clamped between two half-split aluminum cylinders with a PVDF sensor and with a current detection terminal. A dc 20 kV voltage application for 1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex> is repeated with changing in its polarity. Many space charges (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q_{\text{sc}}$</tex>) are accumulated in the cable at every polarity reversal, though total charges (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q_{\text{tot}}$</tex>) calculated from the integration of the current for 1 h decreases with increasing the repetition number. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q_{\text{tot}}$</tex> per unit area at 10th and 11th repetitions were decreased about half of those at 5th and 6th. On the other hand, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q_{\text{sc}}$</tex> per unit area at 10th and 11th were almost same as those at 5th and 6th. These results suggest that the current reduction phenomena caused by the repetitive voltage application with the polarity reversal is not due to the decrease in the absorption current component but due to the decrease in the conduction current component. Temporal changes in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q_{\text{sc}}$</tex> can be roughly expressed with an exponential function. In a few cases, however, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q_{\text{sc}}$</tex> does not saturate within 1 h because the field concentration due to the hetero charge accumulation induces successive charge injection from a heated inner electrode into the XLPE.

articleTitle: Long-Term Partial Discharge Characteristics till Breakdown in a 22 kV Cast Resin Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: This paper presents a long-term trend analysis of partial discharge (PD) characteristics of an aged 22 kV rated cast resin transformer (CRTr) using an accelerated AC voltage of 26 kV at 300 Hz up to breakdown in the laboratory. For comparison, long-term on-line PD measurements were performed in a field using multiple transient earth voltage (TEV) sensors installed outside electric distribution panel where several 22 kV CRTr's were in operation. Under the laboratory accelerated test, the acceleration equivalence of the repetition rate of PD pulses indicated that an acceleration factor of α = 30 could be assumed by multiplying the applied voltage acceleration factor αv = 5 by the frequency acceleration factor αr = 6. Over the elapsed time trl = 6651 hours from the PD test initiation to dielectric breakdown, an increase in PD activity was observed. Calculating the remaining lifetime with α of 30, it was found that the remaining lifetime under service operating conditions would correspond to 23 years. It was also found that the phase-resolved PD pattern exhibited a continuous increase in the maximum PD charge and an increase in the range of phases over which PD occurred. This result suggests that the PDs, which may be generated in void defects in the CRTr insulation system, caused progressive degradation leading to dielectric breakdown. On the other hand, long-term PD trends measured from TEV sensors installed outside the field switchboard showed large seasonal variations, but no significant increase in PD activity. The results at this field suggest that the CRTr in service operation has not yet experienced significant degradation.

articleTitle: Partial Discharge Testing on MV Motor – Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: A failure of a medium voltage (MV) motor during its operation could force an outage of the power plant and also lead to a loss of cost. Hence, the method to ensure the insulation quality of such a motor is needed. Partial discharge (PD) testing is one of the effective methods used to determine the defect and evaluate the integrity of the machine insulation. This paper presents the application of off-line PD testing on MV motors. In the experiment, the PD test instrument conforming to standard IEC 60270 was used as a charge-based measurement. Moreover, during the PD testing, an acoustic imaging camera was employed as an alternative technique for locating the PD sources in the stator winding part. Once PD takes place, it can generate the pressure acoustic wave that propagates surrounding the PD source. Thus, the PD source in the area of endwinding can be located by this technique. From the charge-based PD test results, the phase-resolved PD (PRPD) pattern was considered to identify the type of PD source. It was found that almost MV motors tested have delamination in the bulk insulation. In some cases, the PRPD pattern exhibits the discharge in the area of the overlap region between the semiconductive and stress grading coating in the slot exit, which confirms by using the acoustic technique.

articleTitle: Time-Temperature and Time-Electric Field Correlation for Integrated Currents in XLPE
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Applying a DC voltage to an electrical insulating material such as polyethylene, various kinds of current flow within a sample due to varying physical phenomena. Among them, a conduction current (leakage current) flows in the final steady state which is usually measured by a picoammeter. As the conduction current is so small, noise reduction is a very big issue in measuring the current accurately. We tried to measure the conduction current using the “Direct Current Integrated Charge Method” (Q(t) method) which measures the current as an integrated charge using an integrating capacitor. Integration of the current leads to the accurate measurement of the current as random noises are canceled; in addition, parameters such as Q(t)IV or Q(t)/CV reveal similar figures for voltage or temperature. From this, using the converted time in which a shift factor is multiplied by real time, Q(t) data in different temperatures or electric fields can be drawn by a single curve, namely time-temperature and time-electric field correlation are shown. In this paper, based on the cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) data, a potential time-temperature and time-electric field correlation is revealed, and the physical meaning of the shift factor is discussed.

articleTitle: Partial Discharge Detection and Analysis on a Cast Resin Transformer Under Lightning Impulse Voltage
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The purpose of this research is to understand the partial discharge (PD) activity of an actual transformer before dielectric breakdown and estimate its remaining life. For this purpose, acceleration of insulation degradation is required, and an impulse voltage application is chosen for this work. The paper presents the detection of PD activity under impulse voltages through a differential current transformer (CT) and the evaluation of PD charge using the current integration method and signal processing. AC PD measurements are conducted before and after the impulse application to analyze the effect of lightning impulses on the subsequent AC PD activity. Experimental results revealed that impulse PD activities with a large amplitude of charge occurred at a higher impulse voltage. AC PD inception voltage (PDIV) and phase resolved partial discharge (PRPD) exhibited a significant change due to the impact of PDs under impulse voltage. It is suggested that impulse PDs with a magnitude of uC order can damage the insulation and cause severe degradation in the windings.

articleTitle: Effect of Moisture Content on Temperature Dependence of Partial Discharge Characteristics of Biodegradable Ester Oil
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In our previous studies, we have reported that the relative moisture content of biodegradable ester oil increases with increasing temperature and affects the breakdown voltage (BDV). In this paper, we investigated the dependence of partial discharge (PD) characteristics on moisture content and temperature under conditions of high moisture content in biodegradable ester oil (EO). Toward a corona-free transformer that does not generate PD, in this report, basic PD characteristics were obtained for palm fatty acid esters (PFAE) under AC voltage with varying oil temperature and relative moisture content (RMC) using a needle-plate electrode. The results showed that the frequency of PD generation decreased with increasing oil temperature. It was also found that the frequency of PD occurrence increased, and the average charge decreased with increasing moisture content. We believe that the moisture content (MC) in the oil is the weak point of PD. The partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV) was determined from these PD characteristics, and its relationship was investigated by comparing it with the BDV characteristics.

articleTitle: The Inversion Algorithm of Non-Invasive Surface Potential Measurement Based on Wiener Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Traditional measurement schemes of surface potential are only suitable for short-circuit stage, where the surface potential and surface charge are located on the same surface of the test sample. The non-invasive measurement enables online measurement of surface potential by applying high voltages on one side of the test sample and measured surface potential on the other side, and the sample thickness should be considered when constructing the inversion algorithm from surface potential to surface charge. In this paper, the inversion algorithm in needle-plate configuration is calculated with the analytical method and optimized by the Wiener filter. The Wiener filter weakens the negative oscillation in the inversion matrix, and the surface charge distribution after inversion conforms to the actual situation, rather than the speckle distribution calculated by the inversion algorithm without the Wiener filter.

articleTitle: Observation of Changes in Partial Discharge Activity in Artificial Voids Based on Analysis of $\Phi-\mathrm{q}-\mathrm{n}$ Characteristics and Light Emission Distribution of Partial Discharge
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: To investigate the degree of partial discharge degradation of resins and resin composites due to long-term application of voltage, attempts have been made to determine changes in discharge activity based on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Phi-\mathrm{q}-\mathrm{n}$</tex> characteristics. However, it was not possible to accurately determine the actual discharge activity occurring within the defects from the measurement of the discharge amount alone. Therefore, an attempt was made to analyze the changes in discharge activity by visualizing the discharge emission inside defects and correlating the actual discharge state with changes in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Phi-\mathrm{q}-\mathrm{n}$</tex> distribution. In this study, a spherical electrode/polyethylene terephthalate (PET)/cylindrical void/PET/flat plate electrode system was employed as the artificial defect structure, and an indium tin oxide (ITO) transparent electrode was used as the flat plate electrode to enable direct observation of the light emission during partial discharge generation. This enabled the analysis of changes in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Phi-\mathrm{q}-\mathrm{n}$</tex> distribution and discharge state for investigating the changes in discharge activity. In this study, the changes in the discharge activity during long-term voltage application in a sealed void structure were investigated. The results demonstrated that even under the same void structure and test voltage conditions, protrusions may be generated because of discharge byproducts, and that the discharge occurring in these protrusive structures significantly affected the discharge activity and erosion morphology.

articleTitle: The Influence of Electro-Thermal Aging on Space Charge Distribution in Polyimide Under Square Wave Voltage
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: As the insulation of inverter-fed motor, polyimide (PI) works under square wave voltage, with high frequency and steep rising/falling edge. In order to explore the insulation performance of PI, the samples were subjected to the accelerated aging treatment under the square wave electric field at 200°C. By observing the surface morphology of the samples, it is found that there are obvious partitions in the samples. The breakdown point of the sample is distributed in the region with the combined effect of electrical and thermal aging. Conduction current test and DC space charge test were carried out on the electro-thermal aging region of PI samples with various aging degrees. The results show that electro-thermal aging promotes the increase of conduction current and leads to a slight increase of the threshold electric field. As for the charge distribution in the polarization, heterocharges accumulate near the interface of the sample after aging, which is likely to do with the destruction of the polymer insulation structure. By observing the amount and rate of charge annihilation in the relaxation process, aging increases the density of deep traps in the insulation and introduces deeper traps. Moreover, during the aging process, there is an obvious corona discharge phenomenon in the air gap between the electrode edge and the sample, it is thus worth further exploring the insulation performance of the region where corona discharge and thermal aging act simultaneously.

articleTitle: Discrimination of Insulation Condition Based on Partial Discharge Waveform Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The characteristics of the partial discharge (PD) waveform reflect the behavior of electron avalanches in the discharge space. When an insulator with lower surface resistivity is employed, the difference in surface resistance appears at the rising part of the waveform. In this report, we classified the insulation condition from the PD waveform using deep learning. We showed that learning by extracting only the rising part of the waveform improved the classification accuracy. Furthermore, the frequency band of the waveform was adjusted using an appropriate digital filter, and the relationship between the accuracy and waveform characteristics was shown from the point of view of the difference in the statistical distribution of waveform characteristics. Using the JS (Jensen-Shannon) divergence as an index of the similarity of the distribution, it was found that the rising part of the waveform mainly reflected the surface resistivity difference. This result agrees with the tendency read from the classification test using deep learning. In addition, it implied that it is possible to estimate the waveform characteristic strongly reflecting the insulation condition using the classification test.

articleTitle: Estimation of Electric Field Distribution in a 220KV HVAC XLPE Cable Under Differential Ageing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Inhomogeneous temperature distribution within the bulk of the cable insulation can lead to unexpected conductivity variations at different radial positions of the insulation. Consequently, when estimating the electric field, considering the cable insulation as a homogeneous bulk may not provide an accurate model. In this paper cable insulation is peeled out from 220kV XLPE cable at equidistant radial position from conductor. Volumetric current at 50kv/mm at 40 °C for 1 hour is measured for all layers and conductivity equation is estimated. This conductivity equation is used for estimation of electric field inside the bulk of cable insulation using FEM based COMSOL Multiphysics software. Estimation of electric field based on spatial conductivity has been done and compared with electric field estimated considering conductivity as bulk property of cable insulation.

articleTitle: Identification and Analysis of Micro Defects in Insulation Pull Rod Based on the Ultrasonic Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: During the manufacturing process of insulation rods, internal defects inevitably arise, causing partial discharges or breakdowns under electric field. The detection of internal defects before putting into operation can effectively reduce the occurrence of these situations. Ultrasonic method is considered as an effective method for detecting internal defects with its high efficiency and sensitivity. In this paper, different artificial defect samples are identified based on ultrasonic transmission method detection, and it is found that the internal air defects of fiber-reinforced epoxy composite parts at the millimeter thickness level can be sensitively identified, and the size of the defect area can be calculated based on the waveform and the probe wafer size. The problem of mixing the onset waveform with the bottom echo waveform when detecting thinner parts based on ultrasonic reflection method is solved, and the use of small size probes directly applied to the defect detection of GIS insulation rods is important to guide the operational reliability of insulation rods.

articleTitle: Partial Discharge Characteristics in Twisted Enameled Wires Under High Repetition Voltage Pulses Generated by a SiC-MOSFET Inverter Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: This paper reports the ambient humidity dependence of the repetitive partial discharge inception voltage (RPDIV) in a twisted pair sample simulating the turn-to-turn insulation of a random wound motor coil winding using a SiC MOSFET inverter power supply. The pulse width of the pulsed voltage applied to the twisted pair sample was 500 ns, and the pulse repetition frequency (PRF) was varied from 60 pps to 1 Mpps. At a PRF of 60 pps, the RPDIV decreased by about 27 % as relative humidity increased from 30 % to 90 %, whereas at a PRF of 1 Mpps, the decrease in RPDIV was smaller, about 10%. This humidity-dependent change in RPDIV appeared when the PRF reached frequencies higher than 10 kpps. It is expected that a pulse generator with a high PRF of 10 kpps or higher can reduce RPDIV variations originating from fluctuations in ambient humidity in insulation evaluation tests of actual motor coils, where the ambient humidity is difficult to adjust.

articleTitle: Effect of Carbon Black Addition on Dielectric Breakdown Strength of Alicyclic Epoxy Resins
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: This paper presents preparation of composites consisting of alicyclic epoxy resin and carbon black (CB), and investigation on the effect of CB addition rate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{cb}}$</tex> on dielectric breakdown strength (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{\mathrm{b}}$</tex>). Experimental results showed that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{\mathrm{b}}$</tex> decreased with increasing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{cb}}$</tex>, even by less than half of that of the sample without CB addition when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{cb}}$</tex> further increased from 0.1 wt% to 0.5 wt%. Observation using a digital microscope showed that the CB in the sample was not well dispersed: the particle size of CB alone was on the order of nanometers, while many agglomerates of several tens of microns were observed. As a result, the decrease in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{\mathrm{b}}$</tex> due to the CB addition is considered to be closely related to the size and number of CB agglomerates.

articleTitle: ISEIM2023: Different Dielectric Properties in Polyvinylidene Fluoride
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) has a variety of phases that can be transformed into one another. Each PVDF crystal phase has specific physical and chemical properties for a wide range of applications in the industry. In this work, PVDF membrane with two typical crystalline phases (and) have been prepared under distinct crystallization conditions through dimethylformamide (DMF) solution method at different temperatures. The two crystalline phases were confirmed by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), X-ray scattering (XRD), and polarized light optical microscopy (PLOM). In the range of 70–130 °C, the higher the solvent evaporation temperature, the lower the crystallinity of the film, the higher the proportion of dendritic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> phase in the sample, and the higher the relative permittivity (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon^{\prime}$</tex>). The enhanced amorphous phase polarization and interfacial polarization result in higher <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon^{\prime}$</tex> for films with composite crystalline phases. The dendritic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> phase with a small <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon^{\prime}$</tex> has a lower charge injection barrier, which is consistent with the non-polar intrinsic property of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> phase.

articleTitle: Electric Field Distribution at High Temperatures in Impregnated Enameled Conductors Used in Electrical Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV) is a critical parameter for the reliability of electrical machines incorporating SiC and GaN converter technologies. Most of the machine impregnation resins operate in the plasto-viscous region (above their glass-transition temperature) where large permittivity values can be expected. At high temperature field enhancement in the air surrounding such materials may be expected, potentially reducing the PDIV. In this study, two different epoxy-based impregnation resins with significant differences in contribution to PDIV performance have been compared. For both strong correlation is found among impregnated twisted pairs sample capacitance and flat resin sample permittivity as function of temperature. Simulations of the electric field distribution suggest that PDIV depends mostly on the coating properties of the resin rather than its dielectric one and that a good resin overcoating layer thickness or a buildup of resin in-between the wires are needed to improve the performances.

articleTitle: Effect of Insulation Thickness on Space Charge Behavior and Electric Field Evolution in HVDC Cable Under Polarity Reversal Voltage
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The distribution of the electric field and temperature field during polarity reversal is one of the key factors to be considered in the design of insulation layer thickness of HVDC cables. This study investigates the effect of the insulation layer thickness on the electric-thermal field distribution and space charge behavior during polarity reversal voltage. Taking ±500 kV HVDC cable as the research object, the heat conduction model and charge transport model considering impurity dissociation are established. The results show that as the insulation thickness decreases from 30 mm to 22 mm, the insulation temperature gradient (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta \mathrm{T}$</tex>) decreases while the average electric field and space charge density increase. With the effect of increasing space charge density, although the maximum value of the electric field (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{\max}$</tex>) increases during DC voltage and polarity reversal voltage, the electric field distortion rate (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{\mathrm{E}}$</tex>) decreases obviously.

articleTitle: Electrical Treeing and Partial Discharges in Double Layer Printed Circuit Board
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: With the development of power devices, the demand to improve insulation performance of printed circuit boards (PCBs) is increasing. PCB faces great challenges in its insulation failure caused by long-term ageing when subject to intensive electric fields. It is observed that failures are commonly detected between layers. Therefore, this paper designed and made V-shaped double layer samples to test the partial discharge and electrical tree growth. Based on the method of pulse sequence analysis and phase-revolved partial discharge pattern, the insulation deterioration in layers is analyzed. It was found that the electrical tree grew into branched electrical trees. Based on the PSA, the growth of tree conforms the characteristic of non-conductive electrical tree. The partial discharges inception and extinction voltage decrease at first as the tree grows. But as the electric tree grows, their trend becomes very complex. The apparent charge followed almost linear relationship with the maximum length of electrical tree in the first 5 minutes.

articleTitle: Breakdown Characteristics of Mineral Oil in Uniform to Non-Uniform Electric Field Under AC Voltage Using Bare Electrodes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: It is imperative that insulation designers understand breakdown voltage (BDV). BDV of transformer oil are generally understood to follow stressed oil volume (SOV) theory. However, estimating more than 90% stressed oil volume in non-uniform electric fields in a transformer is extremely time consuming. In this study, a prediction formula that can easily estimate the BDV of mineral oil is proposed. The breakdown characteristics of mineral oil were investigated in a non-uniform electric field under AC voltage application. Experimental results were obtained with those several bare electrodes and oil gap lengths, hemisphere - plane electrodes, rod - plane electrodes, and edge - plane electrodes, respectively. As a result, it was derived that a prediction formula represented by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sqrt{U}E_{\max}=39.2D^{-0.28}$</tex>. It was also confirmed that experimental results matched to the prediction curve and could easily estimate the breakdown voltage.

articleTitle: Effect of Twin Content on Sulfur Corrosion Resistance of Copper Windings
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Recently, the oil-sulfur corrosion of copper winding in transformer has been widely concerned at home and abroad. However, most of the solutions to this phenomenon focus on insulating oil, mainly including strict acceptance of new oil, addition of metal passivator, etc., and the research on copper winding itself is lacking. Herein, grain boundary engineering was used to treat copper windings, and the effect of twin content on sulfur corrosion resistance of copper windings was researched. Copper windings with different twin content (18.2, 41.2 and 61.6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) were obtained by adjusting the deformation of copper. According to IEC 62535 standard, the oil-sulfur corrosion test was carried out. The results show that the corrosion product deposits on copper windings and insulation paper decrease as the twin content increases. Moreover, the large twin content can improve the electrical performance of the insulating oil and insulating paper. The electrochemical polarization curve of the copper windings was measured. With the increase of twin content, the corrosion potential shifts positively and the corrosion current density decreases. This explains the mechanism that increasing the twin content improves the corrosion resistance of copper windings. This work provides useful information for suppressing oil sulfur corrosion in transformers.

articleTitle: Acoustic Emission Characteristics of SiC MOSFET Based on Flexible Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The acoustic emission (AE) signal generated by power devices during operation is an important research topic for non-damage, high-efficiency, and high-precision condition monitoring methods. This paper proposes an AE sensing method for power devices based on the flexible AE sensor, and the effectiveness of the method is demonstrated through comparative experiments on a SiC MOSFET (C2M0160120D) with piezoelectric ceramic sensors. It is found that the AE signals of SiC MOSFET are composed of high-frequency components and low-frequency components, in which the high-frequency components are generated during the turn-on and turn-off process, and the frequency domain characteristics of the low-frequency components have peaks at 250kHz, 310kHz and 370kHz. In addition, the influence of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_{\text{DC}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{\text{off}}$</tex> on the high-frequency components of AE signals is studied. It can be obtained that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_{\text{DC}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{\text{off}}$</tex> have little correlation with the magnitude and peak-peak value of the turn-on signals, but have a strong correlation with the magnitude and peak-peak value of the turn-off signals.

articleTitle: Mechanoluminescence as a Tool for the Diagnosis in Epoxy Polymer
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Luminescence induced by mechanical stress, i.e. mechanoluminescence (ML), has been studied in a cross-linked DGEBA epoxy resin as a function of stress and temperature. The research participates to the understanding of electromechanical ageing processes in insulating materials. At room temperature (RT) and 45°C, before yielding, ML shows an exponential increase vs. stress above a stress threshold. At 65 °C (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>), the ML quickly reaches a plateau. The luminescence below the glass transition temperature is compatible with the Zhurkov's model and the literature and has been attributed to free radical recombination with oxygen after bond ruptures caused by the applied mechanical stress. This study could help better understand damage mechanisms in epoxy materials under mechanical stress and demonstrates a potential way to diagnose irreversible damage in this polymer.

articleTitle: Sterilization Mechanism of Escherichia Coli in Highly Conductive Aqueous Solution by Dielectric Barrier Discharge Treatment Using a Water Column Electrode
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: This paper describes the sterilization mechanism of Escherichia coli in highly conductive aqueous solution by dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) using water column electrode. NaCl aqueous solution, (NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> aqueous solution are used as a hydroponic culture simulated solution for agriculture. E. coli DH10B is suspended in the aqueous solution at a concentration of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> CFU/ml. 100 ml of the bacteria-containing aqueous solution is circulated by a micro pump. A thin water-column spraying from the pump nozzle is used as a ground electrode (water column electrode). DBD occurs between the water column electrode and the glass-coated rod electrode. The number of viable bacteria in the discharged aqueous solution is measured using the colony counting method. The viable E. coli ratio does not changed in the both aqueous solutions without the discharge treatment. In the NaCI aqueous solution, the viable ratio decreases with increasing discharge treatment time and increasing concentration. In the case of the (NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> aqueous solution, the viable E. coli ratio is constant until the treatment time attain the critical value, but then it is exponentially decrease after the critical time. This means that the sterilization of E. coli in the (NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> aqueous solution is produced after a formative process, such as changing in pH of water by the discharge treatment.

articleTitle: Simulation of Space Charge Behavior in Low-Density Polyethylene Under Short Circuit Condition Using a Mobility Based on Disorder Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Space charges in a low-density polyethylene film under a high DC voltage and short-circuit conditions are simulated using a mobility based on a disorder model. The disorder model is one of the negative differential mobility models. In experiment, the velocity of space charges increases after the short circuit. The simulation using the disorder model mobility can reproduce the space charge behavior not only under a high voltage condition but also under the short-circuit condition.

articleTitle: Determination of Repair or Replacement Decision Using the Index of the Transformer DGA
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: DGA (Dissolved Gas Analysis) is widely used as a diagnostic method to assess the condition of transformers. It can detect various types of faults, with electrical and thermal faults being the most common. In this paper, an index for thermal deterioration was used to quantitatively represent the degree of degradation in relation to the operational years. The study also analyzed the patterns of index variations with respect to the operational years, which allowed for the derivation of predictive patterns for assessing the condition of transformers.

articleTitle: Parallel Measurements of Q(t) and Space Charge Distribution in PP film
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: It has been reported that the electrical conductivity properties of insulating materials for cables and capacitors can be measured by a Q(t) meter. It is considered that the Q(t) data contains information of transient charge behavior in the sample. If Q(t) meter can be used to measure not only the conduction properties but also the transient charging behavior in the sample, it will be useful for product inspection and product deterioration diagnosis. For film samples, both Q(t) and space charge distribution p(x,t) can measure. In this report, Q(t) and the p(x,t) are simultaneously measured in a polypropylene (PP) film, and the relationship between Q(t) and p(x,t) is discussed.

articleTitle: Electrical Aging Properties of Polypropylene and Its Polyolefin Elastomer Composites
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Polypropylene (PP) has great electric insulation performance and it is environmentally friendly, which makes it has a great potential to be used as the main insulation for HVDC cables. Adding elastomers is a common way to improve its flexibility, which may bring variation of material structure, thus influencing the electric performance. In this work, the electrical aging properties of polypropylene and its polyolefin elastomer composites were obtained. Polypropylene polyolefin elastomer (POE) composites were made with 20, 30, 40, 50, 60wt% of POE content. The breakdown strength, conductivity and electrical aging lifetime of PP/POE composites with different POE contents were tested. The ageing lifetime of PP/POE composites were tested with step-stress method, and the ageing parameter of inverse power law is calculated. The results show that with the increase of POE content, the breakdown strength of most PP-POE composites decreases. But the 40wt% PP/POE composites have the highest breakdown strength among all the PP-POE composites. The current density and the aging life have similar trends with the BD strength. The conductivity increases with the increase of electric field, and the conductivity of pure PP are lower than that of PP/POE composites. Step-stress tests shows that the total aging time decreases with the increase of POE content. At low field strength, the 40wt% PP-POE composites have a longer aging lifetime than other composites. The 40wt% PP-POE composites show the best electrical properties under DC voltage among all the composites.

articleTitle: Pressure and Electric Field Analysis Considering Insulation Porosity of MI Cable
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In this paper, considering the porosity of the MI cable insulation, the mass flow and pressure behavior in the radial direction were simulated based on the Darcy's law. In addition, the electric field analysis was performed to understand the field characteristics according to the load changes. The results of the analysis indicate that the cavity formation point is likely to be exposed to high electric field based on the concentrated field near the conductor relatively low-pressure during load switching.

articleTitle: Observation of Interfacial Charge Formation Process by Space Charge Microscopy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In high-voltage insulation systems, the space charge that accumulates in the insulation is a problem, as the distortion of the local electric field may lead to a reduction in insulation performance. Generally, insulation design assumes that space charge is not existent. To evaluate insulation performance, it is important to know the difference between the actual electric field distribution and the designed electric field. Space charge measurement is one of the solutions. Space charge measurements of insulators are usually made in one dimension using a film-like sample. However, practical insulating systems have complex structures, so we believe that space-charge measurements with two - or three -dimensional resolution will be required in the future. Therefore, we developed a prototype space-charge microscope based on the pulsed electro-acoustic method. An insulating system was mounted on a polymer substrate, and the signal was acquired by scanning a focused ultrasonic transducer. In this study, we observed a transition in the space charge distribution across the insulating interface between different insulating materials. The electrostatic stress signal generated by the action of the pulse voltage was received by the transducer. Immediately after the bias voltage is applied, signals were seen at the parallel plate electrodes, and almost no signal was observed at the interface between the different insulation materials. At the interface, it was observed that the charge gradually spreads out from the triple junction as if it were growing out of the junction. This is thought to represent the process of transition from the electric field distribution determined by the dielectric constant distribution to the electric field distribution determined by the conductivity.

articleTitle: Understanding the Shielding Effectiveness of Short Carbon Fiber Reinforced MWCNT/ Epoxy Composite on Electromagnetic Interference Induced by Partial Discharges
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Partial discharges (PD) in power apparatus radiate electromagnetic waves in the ultra-high frequency (UHF) range, which can couple with the nearby electronic circuit causing interference in its operation. These electronic circuits need to be shielded from electromagnetic interference (EMI) radiation. The short carbon fiber-loaded polymer composites have gained considerable attention in EMI shielding applications. An attempt has been made in the present study to enhance the shielding efficiency of short carbon fiber-loaded polymer composites by adding MWCNT. The electrical discharge-induced EMI radiation is measured using a UHF horn antenna for the assessment of attenuated EMI radiation. In addition, the mechanical and thermal properties of the material were analyzed through dynamic mechanical analysis and thermal conductivity measurement, respectively. The results of the study indicate 5 wt% of SCF added to MWCNT-loaded polymer composites has good shielding efficiency with high mechanical and thermal properties.

articleTitle: Several Innovative Measurement Methods for Insulating Materials Research
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: This paper describes several innovative analysis and measurement methods that the authors have used so far for research on insulating materials.

articleTitle: Effects of Heat and Radiation on Flame-Retardant and Non-Flame-Retardant XLPE Cables
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The leakage current was measured by applying the current integration method for cables insulated with flame-retardant (FR) cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) and non-FR-XLPE, used as safety-related cables in nuclear power plants in Japan. As a result, it has been clarified that FR-XLPE is much more vulnerable to deterioration due to heating and radiation than XLPE. Namely, after heating and gamma-ray irradiation, distinct leakage current flows in the FR-XLPE cables even at a low electric field. However, the insulation resistances of the cable insulator calculated from the leakage currents flowing through FR-XLPE cables variously treated are several orders of magnitude higher than the value required for electrical insulation of circuits. This means there are no concerns about the insulation characteristics of the cables insulated with both non-FR-XLPE and FR-XLPE.

articleTitle: Muti-Dimensional Functionally Graded Spacer for HVDC-GIS
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In bipolar high voltage direct current (HVDC) systems, gas-insulated metal-enclosed switchgear (GIS) may experience a combination of AC and DC voltages. To enhance the flashover voltage of spacers, this study proposes a synergistic optimization method for the AC and DC electric fields (EF) of spacers based on multi-dimensional functional gradient materials (MFGM), which incorporates both gradient dielectric constant materials <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon$</tex>-FGM) and surface non-linear conductive materials (SNCM), and EF simulations and flashover tests were conducted under AC and DC voltages. The results show that under DC voltage, the EF strength of the MFGM spacer at the high-voltage triple junction by 25% compared to conventional spacers and the flashover voltage is increased by 14.5%. Under AC voltage, the MFGM spacer exhibits a 21% reduction in EF distortion compared to conventional spacers and an approximately 18% increase in flashover voltage. The MFGM spacer meets the requirements for collaborative optimization of EFs under transient and steady-state conditions, and holds great potential for application in DC GIS/GIL.

articleTitle: Proton Beam Writing Fabrication of Micro-Patterns in Dielectric Films for Improving Output Voltage Triboelectric Nanogenerators
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Proton beam writing (PBW) has been realized as a micro/nanofabrication technique that uses a focused proton beam to directly pattern on the materials. At Shibaura Institute of Technology (SIT) in Japan, we have utilized the PBW equipment with 1 MeV proton microbeam to precisely create micro-patterns with different shapes (circles, hexagons, pentagons, squares, and triangles) in poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) dielectric films spin-coated on Cu electrodes. In this work, the micro-patterned PMMA films/Cu electrodes were applied as one dielectric surface of the triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) to generate the electrical energy from the mechanical energy. The results show that the output voltages of the TENG devices were increased by modifying PMMA films with micro-patterns (except the micro-pentagons) and varied depending on the shapes.

articleTitle: Effect of Nitrogen Fine Bubbles on Negative Lightning Impulse Breakdown Voltage and Discharge Propagation Characteristics of Pure Water
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Authors focused on pure water as an ultimate liquid insulating material that is harmless to the environment and has the potential to be used as an alternative to electrical insulating oils. Since the part of insulation properties of pure water, such as volume resistivity and dielectric dissipation factor, are inferior to that of insulating oils, it needs to be improved. It has already been reported that nitrogen fine bubbles (N2 FBs) have the potential of increasing the volume resistivity of pure water. In this paper, authors report the experimental results related to the effect of N2 FBs on negative lightning impulse breakdown voltage (NLI BDV) and discharge propagation characteristics of pure water. Some of the experimental results suggest that N2 FBs may not adversely affect the NLI BDV, discharge current, and time from the camera trigger to strong light emission occurring due to spark discharge of pure water.

articleTitle: Assessment of Surface Resistivity of Insulation System Using Waveform Characteristics of Partial Discharge
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Partial discharge measurement is important for the analysis of the equipment condition by using as a tool to prevent dielectric breakdown. In addition, waveform characteristics of partial discharge, for instance, rise time and fall, can provide some information, such as the conditions of partial discharge occurrence. In this work, the partial discharge measurement is performed to assess the surface resistivity of insulation material using the waveform characteristics. Insulation materials, which are PP (polypropylene) and PMMA (polymethyl methacrylate), are used to investigate. The experimental results clearly show that the fall time of PP is shorter than that of PMMA. The fall time may correspond with the discharge process of surface charge on insulation material, which depends on surface resistivity. From the results, it can be inferred that PP has a lower surface resistivity. The value of surface resistivity is validated by measuring the surface leakage current, and the tendency agrees with our assumption.

articleTitle: Classification of the Aging Condition of Silicone Rubber Insulating Material Using Laser Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy Adopting Recurrence Plot
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Silicone rubber material is widely used as insulation structure in electrical power systems. However, it is susceptible to aging due to environmental factors such as heat, light, and moisture. In this study, silicone rubber was soaked in distilled water and aged at 90 °C, Subsequently, it was subjected to laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) analysis to identify the variation in elemental composition of the sample. The variation in contact angle of the sample has served as a foundation for classifying the aging characteristics. A Grey Level Co-Occurrence Matrix (GLCM) approach is implemented to extract features from the recurrence plot after recurrence analysis of LIBS spectra. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is adopted to classify the level of aging of the polymer based on the features extracted. The proposed CNN-GLCM diagnostic model has shown higher diagnosis accuracy of 98.7%.

articleTitle: Measurement of Absorption Current of Polyester Coated Enameled Wires with Q(t) Meter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: A Q(t) meter is used to measure electrical properties in insulating materials. Here, Q(t) is the integral value of circuit current with time t. It is possible to measure the Q(t) of the insulation material of a capacitor and a cable by using Q(t) meter. The current through an insulating material is divided into an instantaneous charging current, an absorption current and an equilibrium leakage current. It is considered that the absorption current is related to charge accumulation in the insulating materials. In this paper, an enameled wire (1.6 PEW) is used to prepare a cable sample, the Q(t) of the coated polyester (PEs) is measured, and extraction of absorption current components from measured Q(t) are reported.

articleTitle: Investigation on the Effect of Al2O3 Nanoparticle with Surfactant on Electrical Performance of Synthetic Ester Liquid
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Nanofluids with surfactants show uniform dispersion of nanoparticles in the base fluid. In the present study, nano-alumina particles were dispersed in synthetic ester fluid with Span 80 as a surfactant. Uniform dispersion and stability of nanoparticles were ascertained through zeta potential measurements. The performance of nanofluids with surfactant was analysed by carrying out breakdown studies under AC, and lightning impulse voltages. The optimized surfactant-modified nanofluid was observed to have improved positive Lightning Impulse breakdown voltage by 12.5 %, along with an increase in the time to breakdown (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta\mathrm{t}$</tex>). The modified version of Abedian and Sonin's theory is used to deduce the wall charge density coefficient for Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-ester-based nanofluid in a Couette flow using a spinning disk system. The study of streaming current due to flow electrification shows that surfactant-modified nanofluid has higher streaming current as compared to unmodified nanofluid. The effect of temperature on electrification current has been observed within a temperature range of 30°C to 90 °C at different angular velocity. The streamline pattern along with surface velocity magnitude is simulated under different disk velocity and dimension using COMSOL to realize the hydrodynamic condition of flow of nanofluid.

articleTitle: Effect of Electrometer Internal Circuit Parameters in Interpretation of Conduction Current Transient Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Conduction current measurements of insulating materials have traditionally relied on commercial electrometers as the primary equipment. Previous studies have documented diverse current dynamics exhibited by polymer insulating materials when subjected to different voltage and temperature conditions. These current characteristics are closely related to the charge dynamics of the polymers. However, little attention has been given to exploring potential instrumental errors associated with these measurements. In this study, authors address this gap by conducting circuit simulations using a linear equivalent circuit model of dielectrics. The simulations incorporate the internal circuitry of commercial electrometers. The current and voltage characteristics of the measuring circuit and polymers were discussed. Furthermore, performed experiments to replicate the electrometer setup and observed and reported variations in the conduction current characteristics that occur with changes in the internal circuit parameters.

articleTitle: Duration of Current Application Until Outer Semiconducting Layer Started Burning and Temperature Increase across Gap in Samples Simulating Breakage of Shielding Layer in 6.6 kV XLPE Cable Under Constant AC Current
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Breakage of shielding layers is one of the factors for degradation of extruded three-layer (E-E type) 6.6 kV cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) cables. When a shielding layer is broken, a charging current flows through an outer semiconducting layer, and its temperature increases due to heat generation of the semiconducting layer, which can cause dielectric breakdown of XLPE. In the previous study, in order to investigate the detailed conditions under which a temperature increases due to a breakage of a shielding layer in an E-E type 6.6 kV XLPE cable, the duration of the voltage application until the outer semiconducting layer started burning and a temperature across a gap in samples simulating breakage of a shielding layer in a 6.6 kV XLPE cable were measured under constant 50 Hz AC voltages. In this study, the duration of the current application until the outer semiconducting layer started burning and a temperature across a gap with the lengths of 0.5, 1, and 3 mm were measured under constant 50 Hz AC currents, which were assumed to be charging currents of a cable.

articleTitle: Surface Potential Decay and Hydrophobicity of Three Liquid Silicone Rubbers Before and After Direct Fluorination
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Due to many desired properties, liquid silicone rubber (LSR) is the first choice for external insulation of all kinds of bushing in substations or converter stations. This report compares basic electrical properties and hydrophobicity of three commercial LSRs before and after direct fluorination. They are fluorinated in a laboratory reactor with the same fluorination temperature, pressure and time, using the same F2/N2 mixture. This report shows the effect of SR formulation on the basic electrical properties, and further reveals the effect of the formulation on the changes in basic electrical properties caused by the fluorination. Measurements of water contact angles show that the fluorination always results in final high hydrophobicity for three LSRs, regardless of the initial contact angle after the fluorination. Based on ATR-IR and XPS analyses and SEM observation, this report characterizes the physicochemical characteristics of the SR fluorinated layers.

articleTitle: Investigations on the Local Thermal Breakdown in Polymeric Insulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The breakdown of cable insulation., is almost always preceded by a thermal runaway., which tends to initiate at some local spot., which may be the weakest link in the insulation matrix., owing to some impurity., defect or charge trapping. In this paper., the authors attempt to estimate the formation and propagation of local runaway spot and the temperature profile in low-density polyethylene (LDPE) films using thermal imaging., until breakdown., under a ramp-type DC voltage.

articleTitle: Enhanced Breakdown Strength of Polypropylene Film by Molecular Semiconductor Addition
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In the long run, the next generation of smart grid put forward higher requirements on the insulation properties of power capacitors. Therefore, there is an urgent demand to increase the breakdown strength of PP film. In recent years, doping with inorganic nano-fillers was often used to improve insulation performance. However, these methods inevitably led to the increase of dielectric loss and deterioration of mechanical properties, which were not suitable for practical applications. As a result, we proposed an all-organic PP-based composite which mixed by PP and the perylene-3,4,9,10-tetracarboxylic dianhydride (PTCDA) as molecular semiconductor, and also investigated its morphological characteristics and electrical properties in the study. The results have shown that the molecular semiconductor introduced a large number of deep traps in the PP film, thereby inhibiting carrier transport and increasing the breakdown strength. This work proved that the doping molecular semiconductor is an effective method to improve the insulation performance for PP-based dielectric material.

articleTitle: Challenges and Pitfalls of PEA Calibration with Fast Charge Accumulating Materials
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: One of the most used techniques for the detection of space charge is the Pulsed Electro-Acoustic (PEA) method. Calibration of signals is usually done by investigating a “reference” signal, which must be acquired while the material is free of accumulated charge. Often one of the first acquisition obtained from the system during polarization is used. While this is usually a reasonable choice, testing on materials capable of very fast charge accumulation is more and more often encountered, and most of the commercially available systems are not able to extract a calibration signal before charge accumulation. Authors propose a procedure to correctly obtain a calibration pulse in presence of fast charge accumulating materials, with standard equipment. Experimental validation was done on polyimide samples tested at 90° C with electric fields from 10 to 50 kV/mm, capable of fast charge accumulation, demonstrating how to correctly obtain a charge-free calibration pulse within 0.3 s. The results obtained were confirmed by measurements from a custom system with non-standard fast acquisitions capabilities.

articleTitle: A Study of Monte Carlo Simulation for Negative Field Dependent Charge Mobility in Polymer Based on Disorder Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Dynamics of packet-like space charges in low-density polyethylene under high electric fields can be reproduced by using a negative differential mobility. However, the mechanism of the negative differential mobility has not been clarified. In this study, to investigate the mechanism of the negative differential mobility, we perform Monte Carlo simulations of charge motion using the Miller-Abrahams equation in the Gaussian disorder model. The calculated mobility shows a positive electric field dependence in a low electric field region. This is because an increase in the electric field lowers the barrier and increases the hopping probability in the direction of the electric field. On the other hand, in a high electric field region, it shows a negative electric field dependence. Under the high electric field, the hopping probability does not increase and the velocity of the charge saturates because there is no barrier preventing hopping even when the electric field is increased.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of Energy Deposition by Proton in Cosmic Ray for Charge Evaluation in Insulation Materials
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The demand of electrical insulation design corresponding to low air-pressure and/or high radioactive rays is growing, because electrical equipment and power electronics equipment have been utilized under severe environment such as high altitude and/or high radiation environment. The performance of insulation materials under the sever environment is deteriorated by electrical charge accumulation caused by radioactive rays which is the high energy charged particles beams such as protons and electrons. As a first step to evaluate the effect of charging on insulation performance, the energy deposition by protons in insulating materials was analyzed using the Monte Carlo simulation code PHITS in the radiation environments assumed at high altitude and aircraft altitude in this study. From the analysis results, it was revealed that the amount of energy deposition was higher as the altitude was higher, and was 800 times larger at 15 km altitude than at ground altitude (0 km altitude). This indicates that the electrical charge accumulation in the insulation materials can be nearly 800 times larger in the high-altitude environment.

articleTitle: Influence of PD Characteristics Within Motor Windings Exposed to Elevated Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Voltage levels used in AC motor drives is continuously increasing and this paper compares the electrical stress appearing in two different motor winding insulation specimens. The aim is to explore the changes in Partial discharge characteristics to evaluate grade 2 motor insulation for different temperature levels and rise times of the applied voltage as well as influence of overshoots. Here it is discussed how much deviation in properties than can be expected for different insulation thicknesses. The paper shows for example that elevated temperature influences the time lag considerably as well as the inception voltage level, which both influence the PD exposure of the insulation system.

articleTitle: Role of Phase Transition on Breakdown Characteristics of Microcapsule-Based Thermochromic Epoxy Dielectrics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Thermochromic dielectrics can actively report temperature anomalies by color changes, which provides a novel route toward the intelligentization of next-generation power equipment. However, thermochromism is commonly realized from the structural and phase transition of materials, the effect of which on electrical insulating performances is still unclear, restricting their applications in power equipment. Herein, the role of phase transition on breakdown characteristics of microcapsule-based thermochromic epoxy dielectrics (TEDs) is studied. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) results show that the core of thermochromic microcapsules will undergo phase transitions between 50°C and 68°C. The DC and AC breakdown strength of TEDs are both enhanced compared to those of neat epoxy resins in a broad temperature range of 30°C∼90°C, indicating the phase transition in microcapsules will not severely injure the dielectric strength of TEDs. With increased microcapsule content, the DC breakdown strength of TEDs gradually enhances while the AC breakdown strength first improves and then diminishes. The enhanced breakdown strength of TEDs is proposed to derive from the barrier effect at the interfacial regions between the microcapsule shells and epoxy matrix, which could significantly suppress the charge transport in TEDs. The decreased AC breakdown strength under the higher microcapsule content could be ascribed to the raised dielectric relaxation loss from the microcapsule core.

articleTitle: The Impact of Thermal Aging on Mechanical and Electrical Properties of Epoxy/Amine Resin
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Epoxy resin is widely employed as a polymeric insulation material. Epoxy/amine resin is a type of resin that is crosslinked by amine groups, exhibiting improved mechanical properties, better durability, and easier curing process. However thermal degradation is a concern as the polymeric insulation material is prone to heat accumulation during long-term use. Thus, this study aims to investigate the effects of thermal aging on the mechanical and dielectric properties of epoxy/amine resin, along with the associated molecule change. Specimens were prepared and thermally aged at 105°C for durations ranging from 0 hours to 1000 hours. Tensile strength, electrical tree growth, dielectric constant and loss were measured to assess the impact of thermal aging. ATR-FTIR (Attenuated total reflectance Fourier-transform infrared) and UV-Vis (Ultraviolet-visible) spectrometers were utilized to analyze the relationship between property changes and chemical structure. With increased aging time, tensile strength initially rose and then fell, which can be attributed to the formation and subsequent degradation of ether bonds in the surface layer of epoxy/amine resin. The consistent chain scission and oxidation were also observed in the specimen surface. Notably, a heterogeneous degradation was found to appear from the sample surface to the core, with nearly no degradation in the core of the specimen After almost 1000 hours of aging. Moreover, a higher crosslinking degree was observed inside the aged specimen than the unaged one, leading to a higher electrical tree initiation voltage. This spatial inhomogeneity of thermal degradation provides a compelling explanation to the diverse effects of thermal aging on mechanical and electrical properties.

articleTitle: The Risk of Insulation Thermal Runaway in Electrical Machines Used in Traction Electrification
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In this study, electro-thermal aging was conducted on an insulation system model to assess its suitability for electric transportation. A full-size stator model was exposed to thermal stress at 150°C, to simulate machine hotspot, while electrical stress was applied using a square voltage waveform resembling real service conditions. An unexpected increase in dielectric losses within the insulation model, primarily attributed to dipolar polarization in the potting resin, resulted in excessive internal temperatures of the insulation system, exceeding 200°C. These findings emphasize the importance of accounting for dielectric losses in converter-fed machine design to prevent insulation degradation and potential material incompatibilities.

articleTitle: Effect of Polarity Reversal on Space Charge Dynamics of HVDC Cable Insulation at Different Electric Fields
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: HVDC underground cable insulation undergo charge injection leading to space charge formation in the insulation bulk. These injected charges lead to electric field distortion in the insulation. Polarity reversals in the LCC converter-based topology have been observed to further significantly degrade the cable insulation. The reversals affect the charge distribution leading to premature breakdown of the cable insulation. This polarity reversal scenario hence becomes a necessity to investigate and understand the charge transfer mechanism. In this work LDPE planar samples are stressed at different electric fields and subjected to different polarity reversal intervals. The space charge is measured and the charge transfer mechanisms are studied. An attempt to find the correlation between the effect of polarity reversal time and electric field magnitude has been made.

articleTitle: Degradation Mechanism of Photovoltaic Insulating Backsheets Under the Stresses of UV Radiation and Temperature
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The excessive use of traditional fossil energy is a major challenge, as it leads to the global energy crisis and climate change. Photovoltaic (PV) power generation technology opens up new opportunities to address these challenges. While the service lifetime of PV backsheets is around 25 years, a variety of stress factors can lead to premature degradation. In this study, the aging characteristics of PV insulating backsheets under two sequential stresses including ultraviolet (UV) irradiation and temperature were studied. The mechanism of degradation induced by UV and heat were investigated by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). These two methods are used to characterize the thermal properties and chemical composition of the samples, respectively. It can be found that the crystallinity increased after UV radiation exposure. Infrared spectroscopy indicated that there were some changes of chemical groups after UV exposure. Changes in crystallinity are more noticeable after UV irradiation as well as heat treatment, and changes in chemical groups are similar to those after a single UV treatment. In addition, breakdown field strength of samples was also measured in order to provide data support for aging state assessment. This research provides a meaningful insight to explore the degradation of polyethylene terephthalate (PET)-based backsheets.

articleTitle: Statistical Comparison of Degradation Grade and R-Index Based on VLF $\tan \delta$
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: To ensure efficient long-term operation of the installed power cables, it is crucial to diagnose and maintain their thermal degradation status. VLF <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{tan}\boldsymbol{\delta}$</tex> (tan-delta) is a useful method for detecting one of the degradation factors, known as water tree, in cables. There are two approaches to assess the cable's condition using VLF <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{tan}\boldsymbol{\delta}$</tex>: degradation grade and degradation index. KEPCO (Korea Electric Power Corporation) use the degradation index for cable fault diagnosis. However, it may be challenging to make accurate determinations. In this paper, we aim to statistically validate the reliability of using degradation grade as a means of determining cable faults when it is difficult to calculate the degradation index.

articleTitle: Improvement of Partial Discharge Signal Recognition for Power Cable Lines
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The data of the PD alarm record collected from the onsite PD monitoring device can be confirmed and judged as non-PD by engineers, indicating a gap between conventional automatic recognition and manual judgment. The analysis found that the existing recognition mechanism only focuses on the relationship between the amplitude q and repetition n and the phase <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\phi}$</tex> of the detected signals in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\phi}-\mathbf{q}-\mathbf{n}$</tex> or PRPD map. The manual interpretation will also pay attention to the characteristics of the time-domain waveform; that is, in addition to the first wave of the maximum amplitude in the PD pulse waveform, it will also pay attention to the changes in the amplitude, width, number of waves and wavefront of each half-wave, and these factors are not there used as interpreting data for the existing PD recognition programs. To improve the recognition accuracy, a more direct PD recognition method has been developed, which can be according to the signal patterns in PRPD map calculated directly to distinguish the waveforms of PD from noise. The effectiveness of this waveform recognition method has been tested based on field-collected data, PD simulation data of signal generator, and artificial PD data generated by HV tests. It has been applied to the automatic discrimination program of online PD monitoring devices and verified in practical applications.

articleTitle: Space Charge Measurement of Power Module Packaging Insulation Under Square Wave Voltage at Sub-Megahertz Repetition Frequency
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: With the development of wide-bandgap high-voltage power devices with high power density, such as SiC MOSFET, packaging insulation has attracted increasing attention for securing reliability. Packaging insulation of power modules withstands constant unipolar square wave voltages due to the anti-parallel diode of IGBT or body diode of MOSFET, which makes it vulnerable to space charge accumulation. However, it is hard to observe the space charge dynamic behavior under the unipolar square wave voltage since the rising or falling time of the square wave is relatively short, hence the ultra-fast space charge measurement is required. In this paper, a sub-megahertz space charge measuring method based on a high repetition rate pulsed electro-acoustic method is proposed. The pulse generator uses the Blumlein line and SiC MOSFET to form nanosecond pulse voltage with repetitive frequency up to 3 MHz. Then, the transient space charge waveform of silicone elastomer for packaging insulation under square wave voltage with high dV/dt is obtained. It is found the fast rising and falling edge of the high square wave voltage can generate electromagnetic interference to the acoustic-electric signal, which should be carefully handled. The proposed sub-megahertz space charge measurement method can provide references for the research of transient charge transport behavior and failure mechanism of high-voltage power module packaging insulation.

Author Keywords: square wave voltage with high dV/dt

articleTitle: Enhanced Output Voltages of Tribolectric Nanogenerator Devices by Modification of Dielectric Material with Micro-pits
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: A triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) has been emerged as a self-powered source that converts mechanical energy to electrical energy. Typically, surface modifications of dielectric materials with post micro/nanostructures have improved TENG output performance by increasing the surface contact areas. Herein, we propose the embedded micro-pits in dielectric material produced by proton beam writing at Shibaura Institute of Technology for TENG devices. Experimental results show the enhancement of output voltages in vertical contact-separation mode of the embedded micro-pit TENG devices compared to the normal TENG device without the micro-pits. We also introduce the analytical model for the TENG output voltages by modifying the dielectric film with micro-pits.

articleTitle: Study on AC Breakdown Voltage Characteristics of Dissolved Water in Insulating Oils by JIS C 2101
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: We investigated the breakdown voltage of ester-based insulating oils, which are currently attracting attention as a substitute for mineral oils in oil-filled transformers. In this study, dielectric breakdown voltage tests were performed in accordance with the Japanese Industrial Standard (JIS C 2101) using four types of ester-based insulating oils, with approximately 100 measurements, for each oil type. The results showed that the dielectric breakdown voltage decreased slightly when the relative water saturation of the insulating oil exceeded approximately 20 %. Statistical analysis based on the Weibull probability distribution showed that as the water content in the insulating oil increased, the shape parameter decreased while the dispersion between the measured data increased. As a practical consideration, it was confirmed that the relative water saturation of the insulating oil should be maintained below 20 % of the saturated water content in the oil.

articleTitle: Estimation of Surface Roughness Using AFM Image Adopting 2D FFT and Wavelet Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Surface discharge studies were carried out with silicone rubber added with 3wt% nano boron nitride composites. The study innovatively involves the frequency domain image analysis for estimating the nanoscale surface roughness of silicone rubber nanocomposites and thereby average surface roughness can be predicted using it as a texture feature. Five frequency domain parameters were extracted from two-dimensional surface morphological atomic force microscopy images.
