The two-dimensional Fast Fourier transform is used to extract the roughness features in the spatial frequency domain. The 2D frequency parameters and AFM roughness parameters are statistically correlated and correlate well with the experimental results. The prediction is high when the average power spectrum and central power spectrum percentage parameter of the AFM image are used for the regression model. Multi-Resolution Signal Decomposition (MRSD) approach is used to investigate the time-frequency features of surface roughness induced by surface discharges employing silicone rubber nanocomposites in an SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> ambiance at various gas pressures.

articleTitle: Classification of Electrical Treeing Images by Machine Learning of Supervised and Unsupervised Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In recent years, machine learning has been widely applied in the field of materials such as material informatics. There are several examples its application to the development of insulating materials. The machine learning is good at classification, judgment, and prediction. However, there are few examples of machine learning applied to various discharge experimental data in insulating materials. Therefore, we would like to predict the progress of electrical tree in silicone gel by using our data. In this paper, general machine learning was applied to consecutive images of treeing phenomena. These images can be classified roughly 2 categories. Also, the two types of supervised and unsupervised learning were applied. As a result, classification was possible in both learning. In addition, we found that insight the possibility of predicting the progress of electrical tree.

articleTitle: Breakdown in LDPE Due to Water Ingression Under DC Polarity Reversal Stress
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: This paper incorporates high voltage direct current step-stress and polarity reversal stress for water treeing, leading to breakdown. In this paper, water is utilized as an electrode to investigate the impact of water ingression on breakdown. A setup resembling the water treeing configuration is created, wherein a HVDC step-stress voltage is initially applied, and the corresponding breakdown voltage and characteristics are recorded. Subsequently, a DC polarity reversal voltage is applied, and breakdown is measured once again. Significantly distinct breakdown characteristics are observed between the two tests. These findings provide valuable insights into the effect of water ingression on breakdown phenomena under different stresses, contributing to a better understanding about insulation failure and will further lead to the development of more accurate models incorporating effect of polarity reversal.

articleTitle: The Dielectric Properties in Frequency Domain of the 22 kV Underground Cables with Defective Joint
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The failure that occurs in the underground cable systems leads to losses in many aspects, not only in the power system but also in the commercial and business. The most failure location in medium voltage underground cable systems is cable joint and cable termination, where the defects occur from poor workmanship. This paper represents the mean to investigate the dielectric properties of the 22 kV XLPE underground cable system to assess the insulation's integrity of the underground cable system. In the experiments, the underground cable system specimens were prepared by simulating the defects in cable joints, i.e., the iron powder on the XLPE surface and the incision on the XLPE surface; moreover, the underground cable system with the healthy condition joint was prepared to represent the new (or unused) underground cable system. To compare the dielectric properties in the frequency domain of the 22 kV underground cable systems with defective joints and the healthy condition joint, the frequency domain spectroscopy (FDS), the off-line non-destructive test, was performed in this research. From the test results, the dielectric dissipation factor shows a significantly different value in the case of iron powder when compared with the healthy condition joint. It reveals the loss peak on the curve at a frequency of 1 Hz. However, the case of incision on the XLPE surface is almost similar to the healthy condition case. The real part of the complex capacitance of all three cases has a constant value in the measured frequency ranges using the log-log scale. However, the imaginary part capacitance shows the distinct value of all three cases, of which the trends are the same as the dielectric dissipation factor curve.

articleTitle: Mechanical and Insulation Properties of Elastomer-Toughened Polypropylene Ternary Blends for Highvoltage Power Cable Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Recently, polypropylene (PP) has gained considerable attention as a promising next-generation insulation material for power cables, serving as an alternative to crosslinked polyethylene (XLPE), and efforts have been made to make the PP flexible. In this study, we report an insulative PP-based ternary blend with high toughness, in which a high content of elastomeric dispersed phases is distributed in the iPP matrix. The ternary blend is prepared through melt-mixing of the isotactic PP (iPP), polyolefin elastomer (POE), and PE-PP block copolymer (BCP). The tensile modulus of the ternary blend is largely reduced by 228.3 MPa, meeting requirement as power cable insulation material. The ternary blend exhibits a higher tensile strength of 14.1 MPa and elongation at break of 717.8% compared to those of XLPE. Also, the ternary blend shows a high melting temperature of 164.9 °C, whereas XLPE has a melting temperature of 106.9 °C. Interestingly, the ternary blend also demonstrates excellent toughness at -40°C as well as 20°C, whereas the binary blend without BCP shows poor toughness. Moreover, although the ternary blend possesses a large fraction of the amorphous phases arising from the POE, it exhibits volume resistivity and DC breakdown strength values comparable to those of XLPE.

articleTitle: Field Distribution in HVDC Cable Accessories: Shaping Field Control Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Thermal and electrical modelling are key actions in the design of HVDC cable accessories as the experimental means for probing field distribution in such objects are still in their infancy. In this work, based on a conductivity law established from experiments on typical materials that are XLPE (crosslinked polyethylene) and EPDM (ethylene-propylene diene monomer) copolymer, we compute the field distribution in a model of 200 kV cable joint using Comsol FEM software. Alternatives in the design of stress distribution are tested for different kinds of joint materials and different thermal conditions. Although relaxation of the tangential field at hot points along the interface between cable insulation and joint insulation can be obtained, not all the process for the establishment of field distribution is mastered due to the complexity in both the object geometry and in the temperature and field dependence of the materials electrical conductivity. The paper points to the need of optimization tools to identify best conditions.

articleTitle: Analysis of Influence of Various Defects on the Electric Field and Mechanical Stress Distribution of Insulation Rod
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Micro defects may arise in insulation rods during both the manufacturing process and periods of service. A simulation model is created to examine how various defects influence the electric field and mechanical stress distribution within the insulation rod. This model incorporates defects such as voids and delamination. Simulation results indicate that as the breaker closes, the maximum electric field migrates along the axis due to a partial structural movement of the rod into the shielding. Varying defects cause distortions in both the surface and inner electric field distributions of the rod. Notably, delamination defects have a significantly greater influence on the inner electric field compared to the rod's surface. When subjected to static loads, the maximum stress values occur at the connection points between the insulation rod and the metal fittings. Delamination defects have a more pronounced effect on the stress distribution within the rod compared to void defects.

articleTitle: Understanding the Surface Discharge Characteristics with Thermally Aged Ester Fluid Impregnated Pressboard Adopting Fluorescent Fiber Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Surface discharge activity in transformers has an effect to permanently degrade the insulation structure. Early detection of these discharge is crucial for system reliability where Ultra high frequency (UHF) sensor and fluorescent fiber technique show good signal to noise ratio and better sensitivity. An accelerated thermal ageing is carried as per IEC 61125 at a temperature of 160°C. Surface discharge inception voltage (SDIV) and Phase-resolved partial discharge (PRPD) studies have been carried out for thermally aged natural ester oil impregnated pressboard (OIP), by adopting fluorescent fiber technique in comparison with the UHF technique. The optical emission spectroscopy (OES) identifies the emission spectrum of elements during the discharge activity, where a machine learning tool is employed to classify the specimens based on its ageing period. Further, characteristic variation in properties of thermally aged pressboard were analyzed through thermal analysis and solid-NMR studies.

articleTitle: Verticality Online Monitoring (VENOM) for Transmission Tower Assessment Based on Arduino
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Transmission line reliability is very important in an electrical energy distribution system. One of the most important components in the distribution of electrical energy is the Transmission Tower. Distributed locations and various geographical conditions require that each tower stand in solid condition with a strong foundation structure. The condition of the tower can experience deformation either because the soil conditions around the tower are moving, the foundation is experiencing cracks, or due to the influence of the pull from the transmission line which is experiencing anomalies, causing it pull the tower structure. Currently, the assessment method involves measuring the tilt of the tower using a Theodolite tool, which is carried out by visiting the tower and then processing the data using software to obtain the tilt of the tower. This method requires significant effort because each data collection requires measurements at spread-out tower locations and often difficult-to-reach geographical conditions. Additionally, the data obtained is only relevant to the time of measurement, so to get trending tilt data, it is necessary to visit the location tower whenever data is needed. In this paper a transmission tower tilt monitoring tool is designed using Arduino called VENOM. By using VENOM, trending tower tilt data can be obtained online through a website. This tool saves time, cost, and effort, and also provides an early warning system if there is a tower tilt that exceeds the set slope value limit. With this system, the follow-up to anticipate tower collapse can be carried out immediately, ensuring the reliability of the transmission line, especially regarding tower constraints. As a result, the electricity energy channel becomes more reliable

articleTitle: Study on the Surface Discharge Process of Insulators and Its Influencing Factors Considering Quantum Transition
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Outdoor insulators work in harsh environments in power transmission and distribution systems, which are prone to various types of particle attachment defects such as fog, icing, sand dust, and bird droppings. These defects may cause the decline of insulation performance and the distortion of electric field distribution. The operating and environmental random factors will accelerate the evolution of insulation failure, and cause flashover failure in serious cases. The existing research mainly focuses on the experimental test, and there is still a lack of in-depth research on the insulator surface discharge mechanism and quantitative calculation methods of discharge voltage. In this paper, an ionization model of insulator surface particles based on quantum transition theory is established. The influence mechanism of active salt component type and non-uniform pollution on the initial discharge voltage is analyzed. The experimental results show that the calculated results of the insulator surface discharge voltage based on the quantum energy level transition are consistent with the experimental values, which is helpful to promote the improvement of the insulator surface gas discharge theory.

articleTitle: 3D Digitization of Shapes and Surface Conditions for Aged Stress Relief Cones in XLPE Cables
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: On the surface of a stress relief cone installed in a prefabricated joint and termination, precipitate would be generated during long-term operation. The precipitate could lead to affect insulation performance for XLPE cable systems. However, the relationship between the state of precipitate, such as the shape, position, amount, and color tone, and insulation performance has not been clarified. Additionally, photography cannot record the state of precipitate without distortion because the stress relief cone mainly consists of curved surfaces. This paper aims to digitize surface condition of a stress relief cone into 3D objects that can be objectively compared with respect to the state of precipitate and deformation on stress relief cones, which are difficult to quantitatively compare each other by photography. Photogrammetry digitizes the outline and color tone of an object into a 3D object from lots of photographs taken from different shooting direction. In this paper, the stress relief cone taken from the dismantled 275 kV prefabricated termination was digitized into a 3D object with the photogrammetry and confirmed its dimensional error of 1 mm or less. This result confirmed that the 3D digitization of stress relief cones using photogrammetry can be useful for quantitative analysis of the state of precipitate.

articleTitle: Self-Clearing Electrode Containing SWCNT Line for Elastomer
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: An elastomer material can realize mutual conversion of electrical energy and mechanical energy. In a practical application however, any insulation defect in the elastomer may lead to failure of the whole system. Therefore, self-clearing electrode properties are essential and single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNT) have been widely used because of their self-clearing property. However, the complex and expensive process of manufacturing large-area SWCNT film hinders its application and development for industrial applications. In this paper, a novel stretchable and self-clearing electrode configuration using a combination of carbon black electrodes and SWCNT line electrodes is proposed. A pattern of block electrodes is placed on the substrate for energy harvesting. The SWCNT line electrodes are responsible for connecting all the block electrodes with the high-voltage terminal or the grounding terminal. This concept fully satisfies the stretch needs of the elastomer and has extraordinary self-clearing properties. The success of the self-clearing event was observed in the burning of the SWCNT line electrode. Additionally, some key factors, such as how breakdown voltage and electrode parameters affect the self-clearing properties were investigated. It was found that high breakdown voltage, narrower SWCNT line electrodes, a large parallel capacitance in the system and incombustible block electrodes are beneficial to the self-clearing success rate. The use of a hybrid block/line electrode structure is seen as a way to optimize the self-clearing performance of SWCNT electrodes and significantly reduce costs for further mass production.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional Space Charge Measurement of Scaled Cable Joint Model and Signal Compensation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: This study deals with the measurement of space charge in a scaled cable joint model as a step towards its application to full-scale HVDC cable joints. Recently, the new pulse electroacoustic (PEA) device has been shown to be up to four times more sensitive than the conventional method, making it an ideal device for measuring space charge in the scaled HVDC cable joint model. Based on its high measurement performance, we assembled a prototype consisting of a 16-channel piezoelectric sensor array capable of automatically scanning along the scaled cable joint model, making it easier to measure the space charge distribution quickly and accurately. The 16-channel piezoelectric sensor array, each with a 10 mm aperture, was used to scan the cable joint model specimen from the deflector to the steering electrode region. Moreover, the study will show a precise signal processing, including deconvolution, corrections for acoustic divergence, acoustic attenuation and dispersion, and local pulse electrical stress to determine charge density distribution. Whereas the result will identify the build-up of interfacial charge through the use of dynamic 2-D imaging.

articleTitle: Examination of Electric Field Distribution Measured Under 24-Hour Load Cycle Condition
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: This paper investigates the electric field distribution in AC-XLPE cables under a 24-hour load cycle (LC), applied three times at 20 kV/mm, under both positive and negative polarities. Notably, the transient changes in electric field distribution from the 2nd LC onwards significant consistency. The study reveals complex interactions affecting space charge behavior, particularly under LCs, attributable to factors such as the volatilization of cross-linking byproducts. Given the developmental stage of measurement techniques, further exploration is necessary.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Flashover Characteristics of Permittivity and Conductivity Graded Materials ($\varepsilon/\sigma$-FGM) for DC-GIS Spacers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The progressive development of HVDC transmission system has urged us to develop a novel technique in supporting the performance of DC power apparatus. Functionally Graded Materials (FGM) are one of the techniques that allow us to control the electric field distribution within the DC insulation system. Our previous works have analytically revealed that FGM with spatial permittivity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon$</tex> and conductivity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma$</tex> distributions applied to a 320 kV DC-GIS spacer could reduce the maximum electric field under all DC operating conditions. In this paper, we fabricated a cone-type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon/\sigma$</tex>-FGM spacer for DC-GIS and experimentally verified its flashover voltage improvement effect.

articleTitle: Space Charge Distribution Measurement During Electron Beam Irradiation with DC Voltage Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In this study, in order to evaluate the insulation performance of spacecraft surface insulating materials when they are irradiated with electron beams under charged conditions, space charge distribution was measured using the pulsed electroacoustic method by applying a DC voltage to the insulating materials while irradiating them with electron beams. As a result, the charge accumulation within the material was observed immediately after the electron beam irradiation, with charge accumulation occurring at positions corresponding to the calculated penetration depth of the irradiating electrons. Consequently, localized electric field enhancement was observed in the non-irradiated regions, reaching electric field values that could potentially lead to insulation breakdown. These findings suggest the significance of not only surface charge evaluation but also internal charge evaluation in the design of spacecraft.

articleTitle: Structuring Dielectric Interfaces for Enhanced Electrical Strength
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The energy transition towards a carbon-free economy requires an increased expansion of the electrical grid. Applications such as joints, bushing and terminations with electrical potential separation are limited in their electrical strength caused by discharges. Especially in cable accessories involving medium to extra-high voltage applications, where the surface roughness and assembly inaccuracies lead to cavities between the insulation parts are critical for electrical strength. These cavities, if above a certain size, initiate discharges and trigger damage processes of the insulating material at the interface. Controlled surface structuring of silicone insulation material in the micron range based on a wrinkle-formation process introduces a controlled cavity volume between the insulation parts, which reduces the number of failure-trigged cavities and extends the interface length simultaneously. Discharge measurements show a clear tendency towards higher breakdown (BD) voltages for reduced wrinkle-controlled cavity sizes with BD values of 45.9 kV compared to 26.5 kV for an undefined microstructured (rough) and 38.0 kV for a triangular structured silicone. The resulting compressed cavity size was analyzed and used for electric field simulations, which shows the dependency between the structure feature and the field magnitudes. The partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV) measurements indicated a lower voltage for triangular structures compared to wrinkle-controlled structures reflecting the severity of the ionization process.

articleTitle: Investigation of Space Charge Accumulation Behavior by Repeated Proton Irradiation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: There are many high-energy charged particles in space, and when spacecraft surface insulating materials are exposed to this environment, they become charged inside the insulating materials, causing electrical discharges. In fact, since ESD (electrostatic discharge) caused by charged particle irradiation accounts for most spacecraft operational anomalies, it is important to understand the charging characteristics of insulating materials from the perspective of stable spacecraft operation. Currently, surface potential measurement is generally used to evaluate the charged properties of insulating materials by charged particle irradiation. However, when insulating materials are irradiated with high-energy charged particles, they penetrate and are charged inside the insulating materials, so internal charging measurement is essential to understand the charging mechanism. While previous studies on the charged properties of insulating materials have focused on the effects of electron irradiation, there are still few studies on the insulating properties of spacecraft surface materials irradiated by proton beams. In view of the above, it is very important to understand the charging and discharging phenomena caused by proton irradiation of insulating materials. In this study, fluorine-based insulating material (FEP) used in Optical Solar Reflector (OSR) of spacecraft was taken up to investigate the charge accumulation characteristics by proton irradiation. Using an irradiation-type PEA apparatus based on the Pulsed Electro-Acoustic (PEA) method, which is a proven space charge measurement method, we measured the space charge accumulation characteristics of samples under proton beam irradiation. In the previous study, as an investigation of space charge accumulation behavior by irradiation flux, the irradiation fluence was unified, and the space charge distribution inside the insulating material was measured for proton irradiation at each irradiation flux and irradiation time. The problem was that the time required to irradiate a sample at one time was limited due to the machine time of the accelerator. Therefore, repeated irradiation was investigated as a method to extend the irradiation time. The charge accumulation behavior of insulating materials that have been irradiated with protons and then re-irradiated with protons was investigated by spatial charge distribution measurements. The irradiation conditions were 2 MeV acceleration energy and 60 nA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> irradiation flux. One hour after 15 minutes of irradiation, the same irradiation conditions were applied again for 15 minutes. Measurements were taken at 5-second intervals for a total of 30 minutes, 15 minutes during irradiation and 15 minutes after irradiation. As a result, continuity was observed in the charge accumulation behavior at the end of the first irradiation and at the time of the second irradiation. This suggests that the irradiation effect of the first irradiation may have remained at the second stage of irradiation, this suggests that the irradiation effect of the first irradiation may have remained at the second stage of irradiation, and it is suggested that repeated irradiation may enable us to obtain the charge accumulation behavior of longer irradiation time.

articleTitle: Molecular Simulation on the Local Morphology and Electronic Behavior of PE/SiO2Nanocomposite
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The addition of nanocomposites to polyethylene (PE) is proving to be an effective and promising method for improving the electrical and dielectric properties of PE. However, the mechanisms of how such nanoparticles could influence the morphological and electrical properties of PE remain largely unknown, especially at the molecular level. To understand this fundamental aspect, nano-sized PE/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> composite molecular models and their interfaces were employed to study the local morphological characteristics and electrical properties across the interface using Molecular Dynamics and Density Functional Theory. We found that the local density of PE fluctuates within a certain distance between SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and PE bulk as a result of attractive interactions between PE molecules and SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles. The diffusion behavior of PE atoms as well as the Gauche and Anti-Gauche defects distributions as a function of distance from SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> could be attributed to density fluctuations in PE. In addition, the potential barrier between SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and PE was calculated using PBE and PBE0 hybrid functionals for both (1 0 0) and (0 0 1) surfaces of SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Both electrons and holes are subject to potential barriers of greater than 0.97 eV across both interfaces. Our findings provide insight into the impact of nanoparticles on the local molecular morphology and electronic behavior of insulating materials, which may assist in the design of novel nanocomposite insulating materials used for high voltage insulation.

articleTitle: Statistical Analysis of AC Breakdown Strength Characteristics According to Nanofiller Content
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: It is known that the addition of nanoparticles to the insulator improves electrical and physical properties compared to the conventional insulator. In this paper, a short-term AC breakdown test was conducted on a material to which three contents (0.83, 1.25, 2 [wt. %]) of MgO nanoparticles were added to analyze the characteristics of nanoparticles added. Based on the results of the test, the characteristics of each material were statistically analyzed using the Weibull plot, contour plot, and box plot.

articleTitle: Effect of High Relative Humidity on the Thermal Aging of Composite Epoxy Insulation Materials
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In tropical environments, the aging of electrical insulation materials is susceptible to the high humidity of the environment. This work investigates the effect of high relative humidity (RH) on thermal aging of Diglycidyl Ether of Bisphenol A (DGEBA)/Anhydride/Wollastonite composite epoxy insulation material. The aging test at 95°C without humidity control finds that this material exhibited exceptional resistance to thermal aging. On the other hand, high relative humidity significantly accelerated thermal degradation of material via the adsorbed water molecules that attack the ester bonds of epoxy resin matrix, resulting in hydrolysis of the ester bonds. The mechanical strength of material decreased by about 43.4% after hygrothermal aging at 85% RH after 2018 hours under the same temperature. By curve fitting based on the relationship between material mechanical strength and aging times at 95°C and 85% RH, life expectancy at 95°C and 85% RH was 2135 hours. Meanwhile, the Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) absorption peak of ester carbonyl bond (C=O) on the material surface exhibited a correlation with the degradation in the mechanical strength. At the end-of-lifetime point (when the mechanical strength decreased to 50%), there was a 78.6% decrease in the ester bond absorption peak due to hydrolysis and thermal aging. And the glass transition temperature of material decreased from 116 to 105°C, the heat capacity of material increased by 10%, the decomposition temperature of material decreased from 412 to 404°C. As the mechanical test is destructive, this work proposes an easier and non-destructive method to identify the extent of aging by investigating the infrared ester C=O absorption peak of DGEBA/Anhydride/Wollastonite composite epoxy material using FTIR spectrometer.

articleTitle: Calibration of Space Charge Distribution by Frequency-Resolved Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: For the pulsed electroacoustic method which measures the space charge distribution by converting to the interaction between charge and pulse electric field, it is necessary to calibrate the obtained signal as it is affected by the transfer function of the system. The reference signal used at the calibration process should represent the impulse response usually comes from induced charge generated by the bias voltage, and must be free from the influence of the space charge. However, it is impossible to obtain the reference signal when the specimen already contains space charge inside. For this problem, the authors have proposed a frequency-resolved analysis method which correlates the variation of the acoustic signal and the bias voltage, and makes it possible to acquire the reference signal even when the bias voltage changes irregularly. This method is expected to be practical when the space charge dose not move. But it is not easy to be applied when the space charge changes with the change in the bias voltage. The method authors proposed to obtain a reference signal while avoiding the influence of space charge. By correlating the time variations of the bias voltage and the response signal via Fourier transform, it can be determined that the signal component due to unstable space charge, which varies with a finite delay time relative to the bias voltage, has an imaginary component in the spectrum. The spectrum in such a frequency band should be discarded for calibration. The frequency components with DC and imaginary components are excluded from the normalized spectrum. The reference signal for calibration is extracted by using a spectrum component with no imaginary component. In the presentation, its validity will be proved through simulation and experiment with a specimen in which space charge is unstably change with the change in bias voltage.

articleTitle: Insulating Property Estimation Using Q(t) Method of tpPI/hBN Composite Materials Produced by Electrostatic Adsorption Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: A composite material with higher thermal conductivity and acceptable breakdown strength has been developed. An electrostatic adsorption method produced a thermoplastic polyimide (tpPI)/ hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) composite to create a thermally conductive composite insulating material. The flaky surface of the hBN particles was oriented vertically to the sample thickness direction (CMV sample) or parallel to the sample thickness direction (CMP sample). The transferred/accumulated charge amount was measured using the Q(t) method to understand the insulating property. As a result, the charge amount ratio (Q(300)/Q0(2)) of the CMP sample at 30°C is higher than that of the CMV sample. In addition, the temperature-dependent transferred/ accumulated charge amount of the CMP sample was also comparatively higher than that of the CMV sample. This is probably attributed to the tpPI/hBN interface, a potential electrical weak point, and is parallel to the CMP sample's thickness (electric field) direction.

articleTitle: Measurement of Spark Discharge Inception Voltage Using CIGRE Method-II Type Metal-Air Gap-Metal Electrode System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: A minute air gap may become a weak electrical point in an insulation system. A successive partial discharge (PD) in the minute air gap occurs under a low-voltage application. The spark discharge inception voltage under AC voltage (AC-SDIV) was measured by using the CIGRE-Method-II (CM-II) type metal-gap-metal (MGM) electrode system to understand the essential discharge characteristics under low atmospheric pressure. The AC-SDIV in the region of the product of air pressure and void distance (pd product) of 0.3 Pa· m and more almost agrees with the Paschen voltage. The AC-SDIV in the region of the pd product of less than 0.3 Pa· m decreases as the pd product decreases. The tunneling emission of the electron from the electrode due to the high Paschen field may occur.

Author Keywords: CIGRE-Method II type MGM electrode system

articleTitle: A Study on Space Charge and Electrical Conduction Current Properties According to Thermal Stress Period of Insulation Materials for HVDC Eco-Friendly Power Cables
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Recently, HVDC(High Voltage Direct Current) transmission has been increasing. In addition, interest in eco-friendly insulating materials is increasing, and interest in PP-based insulating materials, which are thermoplastic insulators, is also steadily increasing. In this study, space charge and conduction current characteristics were evaluated to study the effect of thermal stress on PP-based insulating material, which is of high interest as an eco-friendly insulating material. The space charge was measured by manufacturing a measurement system using the PEA(Pulsed Electro-Acoustic) method. The conduction current was measured with a measurement system manufactured using the method proposed in ASTM(American Society for Testing and Materials)-D257, and the conduction mechanism was analyzed through these data. The results of the effect of thermal stress for insulating material were obtained by comparing and analyzing the measured space charge properties and electrical conduction properties.

articleTitle: The Effect of Nano TiO2 on Space Charge Behaviour of Silicone Elastomer Under DC Electric Field
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Dielectric elastomers (DE) have aroused a lot of interest from researchers due to their huge potential for application in energy transducers. In particular, silicone elastomer stands out for its excellent characteristics such as softness and flexibility, heat resistance, chemical resistance and insulation properties. The permittivity of most silicone elastomers is relatively small (less than 3), which often does not meet the high capacitance requirements of energy transducers. It is common to improve the permittivity of dielectrics through adding fillers with high permittivity, which will not only change the polarization properties but also the charge transport of the material. Under high dc field, space charge may accumulate in the dielectric, distorting the electric field and thus affecting the breakdown properties of the dielectric. In this paper, different contents of nano-sized TiO2 (5, 10 and 15 phr) were added into PDMS (Sylgard 184) to study the space charge behavior of silicone/TiO2 composites by the PEA measurement system. The effects of space charge accumulation on the dielectric properties of silicone elastomer are discussed. The results show that compared with the PDMS without fillers, the permittivity of PDMS with nano-TiO2 is increased in the low frequency region, the dielectric loss is decreased, the accumulation of heterocharge near the anode is strongly reduced and the higher the filler concentration, the lower the maximum electric field distortion.

articleTitle: Voltage Applied Exposure Test of Polymeric Insulators for Distribution Lines in the Coastal Areas along the Sea of Japan: Evaluation of ESDD (Equivalent Salt Deposit Density) Based on Meteorological Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Polymer insulators are increasingly being used in power distribution facilities because of their superior resistance performance to contamination brought about by excellent hydrophobicity compared to conventional porcelain insulators. However, because polymeric materials are used for the outer cover, there are concerns about degradation over time, and clarifying their long-term performance is an important issue. The authors have proposed a method for predicting leakage current generation using Neural Network model, but the prediction accuracy is degraded in some cases. To solve this problem, we expect to improve the prediction accuracy by incorporating the amount of salt adhered to insulators surface and the state of hydrophobicity of insulators surface into the model. In this paper, a method for evaluating ESDD (Equivalent Salt Deposit Density) of polymer insulator surfaces based on meteorological conditions is discussed, and ESDD is evaluated considering salt adhesion by wind from coastal direction and washing of salt away by rainfall.

articleTitle: Web-Based Simulation of Particle Motion in Ionic Wind Flow Using WebGL
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Web-based simulations are computer simulations through a web browser, which are expected to be used not only for remote work but also for education. We have developed a web-based simulation of particle motion in ion wind flow using three.js that is an open-source JavaScript library for simplify WebGL coding. Ionic wind is an airflow induced by electrostatic forces during corona discharges. In general, finite element method (FEM) is used to calculate an ionic wind. However, it is difficult for the FEM to represent the behavior of charged particles in ionic winds. To simulate the charged particle behavior, we calculate the motion of tracer particles in an ionic wind. The calculation results are good agreement with experimental results using a high-speed camera.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Miniature Surface Plasmon Resonance Sensor Chip Using Polymeric Prism
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: In this work, we present the development of a miniature surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor chip using the Kretschmann configuration. The SPR sensor chip incorporates a polymeric prism made from Norland Optical Adhesive 61 (NOA 61). By utilizing NOA 61 instead of a conventional prism, we overcome certain limitations associated with conventional SPR spectroscopy. We employed the confined sessile drop technique to fabricate the NOA 61 polymeric prism, which offers several advantages, including simplicity, low-cost fabrication, and precise control over lens parameters. A liquid NOA 61 was dropped directly onto a flat circular disk with a 6-mm diameter made of poly(dimethyl siloxane) (PDMS). The sharp edge of the PDMS circular disk facilitated controlled formation and the desired amount of the liquid NOA 61, resulting in the formation of a hemispherical prism. Subsequently, UV curing was employed to solidify the NOA 61, then obtaining the NOA 61 polymeric prism. To complete the miniature SPR sensor chip, 3 nm-thick chromium layer, and 47 nm-thick gold layer were evaporated onto the planar side of the NOA 61 polymeric prism and then mounted on a microfluidic cell fabricated using a 3D printer. The resulting SPR excitation curves were observed in the visible region and exhibited a refractive index independence sensitivity of 885.4 nm/RIU. Furthermore, we demonstrated the capability of the miniature SPR sensor chip to detect nanomaterials.

articleTitle: Estimation of Material Properties Through Charge Transport Simulation Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The increasing use of power electronics equipment in various operating environments has raised concerns about the space charge accumulation in insulation materials, especially in high-radiation environments. In order to ensure more robust reliability of power electronics equipment, it is important to have a better understanding of the space charge phenomena in insulation materials. In this study, we investigated the estimation of material properties related to space charge accumulation through the space charge transport simulation using machine learning. As results, the inverse analysis technique for estimating material properties related to charging through the space charge transport simulation was developed. However, some estimated values of material properties with low sensitivity to the space charge simulation had errors as large as approximately 10% compared to the true values. Therefore, it is necessary to consider improving the mathematical model of the space charge transport simulation as well as applying the inverse analysis technique to actual insulation materials in the future.

articleTitle: Experimental Studies on the Sulfur Corrosion Behavior of Copper Windings in Transformer After Different Processings
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: The sulfur corrosion of copper windings in the transformer can cause insulating performance degradation of insulating paper and oil, threatening the stable operation of the transformer. From the mechanism of sulfur corrosion, grain boundaries of copper windings are susceptible to corrosion of corrosive sulfur in insulating oil, when sulfur corrosion occurs in copper windings. Therefore, the experimental studies on intergranular corrosion (IGC) behavior of different grain boundaries were important. Here, optimized grain boundary character distribution (GBCD) of copper has been considered to be a new effective method of enhancing corrosion resistance of the copper windings by controlling the internal microstructure. GBCD-copper windings have been successfully prepared by optimized processing and heat treatment, which is the same processing of copper windings. After designed processings, GBCD-copper windings of different grain sizes (17.488 µm, 59.985 µm, 133.02 µm) were prepared successfully. According to IEC 62535 standard, these indicated copper windings were oil-sulfur experimented under 150°C in the insulating oil of 500mg/kg DBDS content for 3 days. Different copper windings, corresponding insulating papers and oils were observed and characterized. In addition, the insulating properties of insulating papers and oils were also measured, including the breakdown voltage, dielectric loss, volume resistivity of insulating oil, and thermal conductivity and polymerization of insulating papers. Finally, results show that with the increase of grain size, the corrosion deposits on copper windings gradually decrease, the content of copper and copper element in oil and paper decreases, and the electrical properties of insulating oil and paper improve significantly.

articleTitle: Modeling the Dielectric Breakdown of Nanocomposites Using a Novel Phase-Field Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: With the development of nanotechnology, nanocomposites have gained more attention for their increased dielectric breakdown strength and the potential to improve the reliability of electrical equipment. However, there is still a lack of physics-based numerical methods to study dielectric breakdown mechanism of nanocomposite. In this paper, we present a novel phase-field model that utilizes the similarity between fracture and dielectric breakdown. The model employs a phase-field variable, ranging from 0 to 1, to characterize the breakdown damage driven by the competition between surface energy and stored elastic energy. The phase-field variable evolves in accordance with the laws of thermodynamics, which dictates a minimization of the energy of the system. With the setup of the phase-field model, the influences of SiO2 and TiO2 fillers on the electric field, breakdown strength and thermal conductivity of nanocomposites are further discussed. The results highlight that the electric field distortion in TiO2/epoxy (EP) is more severe than that of SiO2/EP, resulting in an earlier initiation of breakdown damage and lower breakdown strength. However, the stored energy density of TiO2/EP is about five times higher than the SiO2/EP, while the effective thermal conductivities of the two composites are almost the same.

articleTitle: Dielectric Strength and Failure Mechanism of Power Module Packaging Insulation at Ultra-High Temperature
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Stricter requirements have been proposed for the safety and reliability of the power module packaging insulation as the development of power devices towards miniaturization., higher frequency., and higher power density. The dielectric insulating performance at high temperatures is one of the key measures for the reliability of packaging materials. This paper investigated the dielectric strength of the two crucial packaging insulating materials.,i.e.., encapsulation elastomer and alumina substrate., from normal to ultra-high temperatures. The thermodynamic properties of the prepared double-component vulcanizable silicone elastomer (RTV-2) were studied for the verification of its thermal stability. Then DC breakdown strength and broadband dielectric spectrum were detected for both elastomer and ceramic in a wide temperature range from 293.15 K to at least 453.15 K. The broadband dielectric spectrum showed that the dielectric loss of the elastomer <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">was</sup> very small., mainly composed of the interfacial polarization and the conductance loss. Conductance loss was also dominant in ceramics. The DC breakdown results showed that the breakdown strength of both two materials maintained basically stable at different temperatures. The critical DC breakdown strength of the silicone elastomer was about 60 kV/mm., and that of the alumina ceramic was about 80 kV/mm.

articleTitle: In a Search for Reliable Methods to Evaluate Resistance to Electrical Treeing in Materials for HVAC and HVDC Cable Insulations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials (ISEIM)
abstract: Research activities are reported on developing a new type of test objects and procedures for evaluating the resistance to electrical treeing in various materials for HVAC and HVDC cable insulations. A test object with wire electrode is introduced and its advantageous features are elucidated. One of them is a capacity to form multiple trees in a single test object that significantly increases the amount of data for statistical analyses. Focus is also made on the possibilities to electrically detect electrical initiation and development of electrical trees. A hypothesis is formulated and evidenced that the resistance to formation of electrical trees in materials for DC applications can successfully be tested with time varying voltages of sinusoidal and pulsed types. In addition, electrical treeing tests are reported on specimens cut from a real HVDC cable insulation that aimed to imitate the cable operating environment and the impact of voltage transients appearing during cable joint failures. It revealed that such transients have a certain impact on the insulation resistance to electrical treeing.
